title: Bad Bunny Opens "Cerramos en Casa" Homecoming Finale at Hiram Bithorn Stadium
detail: Bad Bunny played the first of two sold-out "Debí Tirar Más Fotos – Cerramos en Casa" shows at Estadio Hiram Bithorn in San Juan, closing out the record-breaking, $467.5 million-grossing Debí Tirar Más Fotos World Tour in the city where it launched. Roughly 30,000 fans packed the venue, which underwent an approximately $39.6 million renovation funded by the Municipality of San Juan ahead of the shows. The night capped weeks of buildup — from sponsor teasers and stadium construction in early August, to the official Aug 17 announcement, the Aug 19 ticket sellout, and the city's transportation and security operation — with a second closing show set for Aug 23.

title: Bad Bunny Delivers Fiery Water-Crisis Speech, Calls Puerto Rico's Troubles "Created on Purpose"
detail: Opening night one of the "Cerramos en Casa" tour-closing shows, Bad Bunny took the stage at 6:50 p.m. in light blue alongside Los Primos and immediately addressed Puerto Rico's water and power crises: "I can't bring water to those who don't have water. I can't bring electricity to people whose power goes out every day... What I want to bring you today is hope and strength to fight and continue to defend this land." He went further, framing the island's dysfunction as deliberate: "This chaos, this disaster is created on purpose to try to play with our emotions, to try to give up, to leave, so they can continue to sell this island part by part and fulfill its mission of a Puerto Rico without Puerto Ricans." Opening act Chuwi used their song "Tierra" to raise the same water-and-electricity grievances, then flashed a message on the stadium screens urging fans to join a 2 p.m. demonstration against the ~$2 billion Proyecto Esencia luxury resort and residential megaproject planned for 2,000 acres and three miles of coastline in Cabo Rojo. Bad Bunny also called for the resignation of Puerto Rico Governor Jenniffer González. The remarks drew online backlash from some fans who argued a wealthy global star built on Puerto Rican identity should do more than speak from a stage — "He makes millions but can't help the PR? He should be cancelled," one critic wrote — while defenders countered that responsibility for the utilities crisis belongs to the government, not an artist.
